newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN staff ambushed in Zaire - UN official.
newsitem.headline: UN staff ambushed in Zaire - UN official.

text.p: Local staff members of the U.N. refugee agency have been ambushed in the anarchic eastern Zairean town of Bukavu and there are casualties, a senior U.N. official said on Thursday, quoting unconfirmed reports.

Augustine Mahiga, coordinator of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for Africa's troubled Great Lakes region, told Reuters in Geneva the employees were attacked while they were trying to flee the lakeside town.

"We have unconfirmed reports that some of our local staff from Bukavu who were trying to leave the town ran into an ambush. We've heard of casualties -- dead and wounded -- but we don't know the numbers, we don't know the location," he said, adding: "The situation is getting very messy."

"The most urgent step needed is to secure a ceasefire. And this is beyond the initiatives of humanitarian agencies. It has to come from the United Nations, from countries in the region and from the whole international community."
In the town of Goma further north, Mahiga said the UNHCR would evacuate staff members following an outbreak of fighting between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi fighters.
"There are reports the fighting is getting closer to Goma town. Our staff are all indoors, either in hotels or in offices. We're making plans to evacuate them," he said.
He said the evacuation would be by land across the Rwandan border to the town of Gisenyi. There are 14 UNHCR expatriate staff members in Goma and another 90 with Western aid agencies.

The UNHCR is the coordinating agency for Goma and is also responsible for security there. If it pulls out, other agencies are certain to follow, leaving more than 700,000 Rwandan Hutus in the region to their fate.
The Hutus fled for fear of reprisals for the Hutu-led genocide of half a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates in 1994.

If fighting spreads, the refugees in Goma would have two escape routes -- to Rwanda where many fear revenge for the genocide, or the Masisi region near Goma, another ethnic war zone where native Zairean tribes are battling local Hutus.
Mahiga said it was impossible for relief agencies to continue work in the absence of a ceasefire.
"Security is the major constraint. We cannot imagine what will happen to the refugees if there is no assistance. It is really going to be a disaster, a humanitarian catastrophe."
